speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific location of your neck and arm pain, and tell me exactly where you feel the paresthesias (tingling or numbness). Do you notice any muscle weakness in your arms or hands?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, are your symptoms worse with neck extension or rotation, and do you have any numbness in your legs or balance issues? Additionally, have you experienced any loss of bowel or bladder control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The patient's presentation of progressive weakness, fasciculations, absent reflexes, and specific hand involvement is highly characteristic of ALS. The previous suggestion of a urinary tract infection is clinically inconsistent with these neurological findings. While the motor vehicle accident history raises the possibility of post-traumatic cervical myelopathy, the presence of fasciculations and upper motor neuron signs alongside lower motor neuron signs in the hands strongly points to a motor neuron disease. Do you have any other medical conditions or family history of neurological disorders? REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI, EMG_results
